gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Tenergy's TN480U charger kits come with no wall adapter (Tenergy: 'Micro-USB to AC power adapter is NOT included'), that the charger needs a DC 5V 2A supply, and that Tenergy's own 20 W USB-C PD brick has only a USB-C port and no cable, while the brick that fits is Tenergy's 18W kit (P/N 59088), rated 5V 2A and sold with two USB to Micro USB cables.
standout_why: I compared six of the pages. geekchamp.com/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-aa-and-aaa-devices-2026 (cited) only gives the general rule: don't put 1.5V lithium cells in a NiMH-only charger. It says nothing about power adapters, input amps or cable type. ikea.com STENKOL/LADDA (cited) has a charger with a built-in wall plug and says it charges only NiMH cells of at least 1000 mAh (AA) or 500 mAh (AAA), so the adapter problem doesn't arise there. d3j1zw3ygsdrnm.cloudfront.net/best-aa-aaa-battery-chargers says 'No wall adapter comes in the box' for a different charger (POWEROWL 8-Bay), gives no input current and doesn't cover the TN480U, so it has part of the idea. gomyreview.com says nothing about adapters, input or cables. None of the pages names the TN480U's 5V 2A input or the Tenergy brick and cable that match it. A shopper who buys only the combo can't plug it into a wall, and one who adds Tenergy's 20 W USB-C brick gets no cable with it.
kit_items: Batteries and charger: Tenergy combo P/N 91257, which is the TN480U 8-bay LCD charger with 8 Premium Pro AA (2,800 mAh) and 8 Premium Pro AAA (1,100 mAh). The charger lists NiMH/NiCd chemistry and charges AA at 500 mA and AAA at 250 mA per slot, so these NiMH cells match it.

Wall power: Tenergy 18W Fast USB Charger Combo Kit (P/N 59088). Its wall charger gives 5V 2A, the same as the TN480U's rated input of DC 5V 2A. It comes with two 6 ft USB to Micro USB cables, which fit the TN480U's Micro USB input. Don't use Tenergy's USB-C PD 20W (P/N 59149) in its place: it has a USB-C port only and no cable.
